summary: The paper adds model/task-specific evidence of amplified demographic and moral preferences and version-dependent changes. No new construct is required. Its parameter-size correlation and average-human distance do not establish causal moral improvement, universal cultural alignment or readiness for safety-critical driving.

findings.term: Some model moral preferences exceed the human reference in magnitude
findings.definition: Several model configurations show same-direction but larger-magnitude attribute effects than the historical human benchmark on text-only MoralMachine choices.
findings.novelty_rationale: Directly extends existing amplification evidence rather than minting another utilitarian-bias synonym or treating each model family as a distinct behaviour.

findings.evidence_scope: GPT4discussion reportsSpecies/numberAMCE>.9versus≈.6human, Gender≈.4versus≈.1, RelationtoAV≈.5versus≈.1. Model families differ, sometimes reverse direction, and updates need not reduce distance. Exact supplementary matrices were not supplied, and narrative human-reference values vary.
findings.boundary: Amplification is relative to the chosen sampled preference vector, not a moral ground truth. Stronger life-preservation weights can be defensible in some tasks, while demographic criteria can be impermissible even when they match popular preferences. This does not establish an internal utilitarian motive, a causal training source or amplified bias across every model/task.

findings.term: Demographic attributes shape reported MoralMachine choices
findings.definition: Gender, age, perceived fitness and social-status attributes have model-specific effects on hypothetical collision choices, sometimes exceeding or reversing the corresponding human effects.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds a direct demographic-output example to existing social bias rather than separate IDs for every affected attribute.
findings.evidence_scope: Across52selected model configurations, reported AMCE patterns differ in sex/gender, perceived fitness and status. Hypothetical descriptions mix social and contextual factors; source prose contains inconsistent humanGenderbaseline(.1inmostpassages,.3inClaudeparagraph), so exact magnitude requiresS1verification.
findings.boundary: A demographic output association is not a measured unconscious attitude or proof of a common psychological mechanism. Human majority preference is not a fairness standard. The source does not test real collisions, legal compliance, affected-group outcomes or a causal contribution from actual training corpora.

methodological_limits: Filename2025corresponds to a later publication; the supplied text is2024arXivv2. Record the version actually read, while linking later metadata without claiming publisher corrections were inspected.

The52configurations are selected prominent models/versions, not52independent architectures or a random sample of all available models. Related snapshots share weights, training pipelines and providers.
Legacy outputs from the earlier four-model study are explicitly reused. This expansion is not a fully independent replication of every reported model effect; do not multiply the reused completions.
Scenario counts differ50000/10000/5000and model-specific default generation settings differ. Precision, invalid-output selection and sampling comparability require full configuration/output records.
Valid-response rates and exactAMCEs are only described in externalS2/S1tables, absent from this suppliedPDF. No comprehensive per-model rate, denominator or query total is fabricated.

Binary forced choices can collapse refusal, misunderstanding, label order and value preference. No systematic equivalent-prompt/option-order or repeated-generation robustness analysis is documented in the supplied main text.

AMCE identification relies on randomized attribute design and estimand assumptions. The statement that the approach needs no modeling assumptions does not remove constraints, selection, interference or weighting issues.
Euclidean distance across nine attributes embeds equal weighting and scale choices. It summarizes the aggregate vector, not the distribution of individual moral judgments or rare harmful outputs.
Original human benchmark uncertainty, sampling selection and cultural variation are not propagated as a matched contemporary human control.

Descriptive human values vary within the narrative:Genderusually≈.1butClaudeparagraphuses.3;Law.3/.4andnumber.6/.7also vary. Approximation may explain some differences, but exactS1values are needed before relying on quantitative amplification estimates.

Some AMCE differences are described as significant without a separately reported interval/test in those family narratives. Larger point estimates do not automatically demonstrate statistically distinct preferences.

The open-source size correlationrho−.54,p.0076is observational and moderate, with counterexamplesLlama3.2 1Bbetterthan3B. It does not isolate parameter count from training, data, architecture, instruction tuning or version.
Base and dialogue-tuned models, MoE and dense models and multiple family snapshots are pooled. Total versus active parameters and shared-family dependence can affect size inference.
Wilcoxonp.92forlargeopenmodelsversusproprietaryis not an equivalence test or proof matching moral capabilities. Thelarge-modelsubsetoverlaps the all-open group; these are not three disjoint groups.
Claiming size is the primary explanatory factor from group medians and a correlation exceeds a controlled comparative causal analysis; proprietary sizes are excluded as undisclosed.

Version-update comparisons do not hold training data, inference settings, architecture and size constant. Nonmonotonic distance is a useful descriptive result, not evidence of agent goal drift during a task.
Figure6visually labelsPC1=47.1%,PC2=27.3%(sum74.4%), whereas prose gives46.1%/28.1%(sum74.2%). This is a publication discrepancy beyond a simple common rounding convention.
Prose saysGemma2 2B/9Bhave largepositivePC2scores; Figure6shows them atstrongnegativePC1andnear-zeroPC2. Some plotted cluster descriptions therefore do not match the supplied figure.
PCA signs are arbitrary and two-dimensional proximity drops aboutonequarterofvariance. Visual clustering is not independent confirmation of a metric derived from the same vectors.
Training-data Western-utilitarian explanations are hypotheses; no actual corpus audit or causal training intervention was performed.

Language/culturaldivergence is discussed largely through cited studies; this experiment uses one globally aggregated human benchmark and does not directly sample multiple human cultures/languages as matched conditions.
Stronger preference for saving more lives is one dimension of utility-related choice, not a complete general utilitarian philosophy or proof of internal moral deliberation.
Matching historical human discrimination is not ethical improvement. The paper itself invokes equal treatment guidelines; distance-to-human and fairness can conflict.

Real-time latency, perception/control robustness, collision probabilities, road rules, actual safety and legal deployment requirements were not measured. More human-like vectors do not establish suitability for autonomous driving.
External data/code/supporting tables and the2025publisher text were not independently reviewed or reproduced; unresolved figure/table and narrative discrepancies stay explicit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This paper explicitly reuses the earlier Takemoto model outputs while adding configurations. Count it as a distinct expanded study, not an independent recollection of the same four-model evidence; retained amplification concept covers both.

The later scaling-law study expands this observational size/distance approach. Neither source establishes that changing parameter count alone causes moral improvement or that distance from one average predicts deployment safety.

Barabadi's context-dependent single outputs and this many-scenario aggregate differ in scope. Neither justifies a universal all-context utilitarian-bias claim; preserve scenario and metric definitions.

Both papers contain figures/prose that disagree on quantities or preference directions. Use verified statedpayoffs/axisvalues and retain unresolved conflicts rather than selecting the version that best supports a desired conclusion.

deferred.reason: Version-dependent output differences are descriptive model comparisons, not an agent drifting from instructions during one task; no new named causal mechanism isolated.
Observational model-size correlation, not a new behaviour or controlled scaling intervention. More explicit later analysis was already reviewed.
A historical protective rule cited as an explanation; no primary norm study or causal mediation test here, and individual attributes already belong to demographic-output evidence.
